title: Platform ops standup - breadcrumbs - 2026-09-09
content:
PLATFORM OPS STANDUP — BREADCRUMBS (2026-09-09)

Attendees: Ethan (owner), Lena, Priya, Jordan, Marcus, Kelsey (joined late)
Duration: 25m (quick-fire)
Location: #pltfm-ops standup -> notes captured here for handoff

PURPOSE
- Rapid sync for control plane, routing experiments, auth rotations, and quota enforcement windows.
- Capture decisions and handoff action items (short-lived meeting notes, will be cleaned into runbook where needed).

QUICK HIGHLIGHTS
- Control plane controlloop latency: p99 rose to ~180ms after kube rollout 9/8; mitigated by scaling controller replicas (PLAT-5823).
- Routing policy canary for small tier customers rolled to 10% traffic; initial metrics look good (error < 0.1%).
- Auth token rotation script (AUTH-129) partially complete; we hit a perf regression on verification path in staging.
- Soft quotas enforcement scheduled for 09-12; need to verify billing + client-facing messaging.

NOTES / DISCUSSION ITEMS
1) Control plane health (Ethan)
- Timeline: rollout of kube-controller v2.7 happened yesterday (09-08). After rollout we saw an uptick in control loop p99 and CPU on the leader node.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): leader lease jitter plus a small goroutine leak in the new watch reconciler.
- Immediate mitigation: increased controller replica count from 3->5, enabled the old reconciler feature-flag on a small subset of clusters. That brought p99 down to ~95ms within 30m.
- Follow-ups: Marcus to file a small profiling PR, correlate GC pause times with controller pod restarts. Link: PLAT-5823.
- Decision: keep replicas at 5 for the next 48h and observe; if stable, revert to 3 and increase probe intervals.

2) Routing experiments and fallback policy (Lena)
- Canary: new routing weight bucket algorithm ON for tier-sme customers at 10% traffic (ROUTE-214). Metrics after 6h: 0.06% increased latency at 99th for short requests (<64 tokens), no increase in error budget.
- Oddity: we saw a cluster where weight bucket underflowed and triggered fallback to default route more often; likely due to stale metrics window.
- Action: Jordan to add a conservative smoothing window and release patch (small param change) tomorrow morning.
- Risk: If we proceed aggressively to 30%, we may trigger autoscaler thrash in certain pools — need SRE sign-off.

3) Auth rota and token rotation (Priya)
- AUTH-129: token rotation end-to-end test failing in staging after enabling HMAC verification cache. Perf regression observed: token verification p50 doubled under concurrency ~200.
- Hypothesis: cache lock contention. Priya ran a single-node repro and saw lock contention in verification.go:scryptCache.
- Short-term: disable cache for verification in staging to resume tests. Long-term: replace global lock with sharded lock or LRU with concurrent hashmap.
- Action: Priya + Jordan to draft patch; target small PR by EOW. Also update runbook note about token rotation rollback steps.

4) Quotas enforcement window (Marcus)
- Soft enforcement goes live 2026-09-12 02:00 UTC for new customers (internal pilot). Need last-minute checks: billing metering alignment, prometheus alerts, and client-facing doc updates.
- Outstanding: missing example email text for customers who hit soft quota; Kelsey will draft and route to policy for approval.
- Action items: Marcus to run the dry-run sim with the billing team on 09-11. Add a temporary dashboard tile for quota overage by customer tier.

5) Incident recap: small routing failure 09-07 11:12 UTC (post-mortem link)
- Short summary: one routing cache rebuild job ran unexpectedly long and OOMed a worker, causing ~12m of degraded routing responses for a single shard.
- Learning: job resource requests were too low and no circuit-breaker on rebuild.
- Mitigation implemented: increased job resources and added circuit breaker with max-run-time 8m.
- Follow-up: add a health-check that will mark job-failed if runtime > 7m and trigger a lighter-weight rebuild flow. Jordan owns.

DECISIONS MADE
- Keep controller replicas at 5 for 48h (observation window).
- Disable HMAC verification cache in staging until lock contention fix is merged.
- Add smoothing window to weight-bucket routing logic before percent increase.

ACTION ITEMS (owners + due dates)
- Marcus: Profiling PR + GC correlation for controller leak (due 2026-09-11) [PLAT-5823].
- Jordan: Smoothing window param patch for routing canary (due 2026-09-10) [ROUTE-214].
- Priya & Jordan: Sharded lock proposal and small verification fix (PR targeted by 2026-09-17) [AUTH-129].
- Kelsey: Draft customer email for soft quotas (due 2026-09-10).
- Marcus: Dry-run billing sim for quotas (run on 2026-09-11).
- Jordan: health-check + lighter rebuild flow for routing cache job (due 2026-09-14).

PARKING LOT / NOTES TO SELF
- Consider a metric that ties controller reconciler # of events per second -> p99 latency to get early signal for reconciler overload.
- Revisit autoscaler config for routing pools after we complete canary to avoid thrash during ramp.
- Note: customer tenant X (acct: tx-338) saw repeated rate-limited 429s yesterday; Marcus to follow up.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS
- Is the default smoothing window (30s) adequate for spikes with high token variance? Need to validate with synthetic workload.
- If we permanently increase controller replicas, what's the cost delta for Dedicated customers (estimate needed).

REFERENCES & LINKS
- Post-mortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Routing+Cache+Rebuild+Postmortem
- Jira queue: PLAT-5823, ROUTE-214, AUTH-129
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/348

NEXT MEETING / HANDOFF
- Next quick sync: 2026-09-10 09:15 PT (focus: routing canary progress + auth perf).
- If anything regresses, ping #pltfm-ops and create an incident with 'controlplane' template.

RAW NOTES (scratchpad style)
- profiling mem growth: look at pprof + tcpdump for leader election chatter.
- Kube rollout cadence: maybe pause next non-critical rollout until we've observed 72h post-rollback.
- TODO: update Confluence runbook with controller replica scaling steps and cost note.

-- Ethan
